changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 4 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/11082-detail-undo-capture.md`

- names `packages/core/src/actions/__tests__/captureUpdateUndoData.export-11082.test.ts` → `packages/core/src/actions/__tests__/captureUpdateUndoData.export-11082.test.ts` — edited by this change

  > Pinned in `packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.undoCapture-11082.test.tsx` and `packages/core/src/actions/__tests__/captureUpdateUndoData.export-11082.test.ts`.

### `.changeset/7997-detail-view-related-retired.md`

- names `RecordDetailView.tsx` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **Why it retired.** `@objectstack/spec` declares no `DetailView` schema at all — every `DetailView` occurrence in `packages/spec/src` is prose about this repo's own `RecordDetailView.tsx` — so this array mirrored no protocol schema and drifted freely: it declared `columns` as `TableColumn[]` while the renderer it fed also accepted bare field names, `{ field, label }` and legacy `{ name, label }` spellings. The axis that carried the ruling was measured **zero pull**: no application code authored the member, both internal producers of a `detail-view` node (`RecordDetailDrawer`, `renderers/record-details.tsx`) synthesize it without `related`, and the only in-tree authorings carrying real columns were two documents — both rewritten here.

### `.changeset/8318-jsdoc-default-tag-corrections.md`

- names `core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts` → `packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts` — edited by this change

  > - `CRUDDialogSchema.size` / `.closeOnOutsideClick` / `.closeOnEscape` / `.showClose` — there is no `register('crud-dialog'` anywhere, so no node of that type ever reaches a renderer. Recorded once on the interface. Per key, the name census differs: two spellings occur nowhere outside the declaration and its zod twin, and `showClose`'s one other occurrence (`renderers/overlay/drawer.tsx:38`) belongs to `DrawerSchema`. - `ActionSchema.level` — `type: 'action'` is not a rendered node type, and `core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts`, which is what makes `method` / `chainMode` / `reload` / `close` live, does not read `level`. - `CardSchema.variant` — `card` IS registered, twice, and neither registration reads it: the `ui` route forwards the key to `ui/card.tsx`, which spreads onto a `div` and mentions `variant` nowhere, and the `page` route forwards only its designer props. - `PageNodeSchema.isDefault` — `page` IS registered, and `PageRenderer` neither reads the key nor forwards it: the wrapper element gets `toDomProps(props)`, an allow-list that does not carry it.

### `.changeset/action-keys-warning-text-5642.md`

- names `ActionRunner.ts` → `packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts` — edited by this change

  > Both halves of the message's tail had outlived the change they described. It told the author the key was warned about rather than rejected because `ActionDef` "still carries `[key: string]: any`" — objectstack#4075 step 3 deleted that index signature, and `actionKeys.pin.test.ts` pins the deletion in the opposite direction (`{ ActionDef: false, ActionContext: true }`), while `actionDef-closed-surface.test.ts` pins that `tsc` now rejects exactly such a key at the construction site. And it prescribed promoting the key to an explicit field on `ActionDef` "(packages/core/src/actions/actionKeys.ts)" — that file holds the INVENTORY (`ACTION_DEF_KEYS`); the interface is in `ActionRunner.ts`. The wrong pointer had teeth: an author who followed it edited the inventory alone, which is precisely the half-change the pin test reddens on, since it re-derives the inventory from the interface's AST.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `9fd6c2c6f` (merge-base with origin/main): 8 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1765 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2371 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36624951969)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `728dd4ca32372f609a96969035e7cb84952277fa`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card objectui#11122 (body; triage `5895671250`; claim `5895849357`; os-dev-report `5897588256`), PR objectui#11137 (body, its 9 files, the net diff against `main`), the head's check-runs (`filter=latest`), and `contents/PATH?ref=` reads at the head of `ActionRunner.ts`, `predicate-record.ts`, `expand-fields.ts`, `useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx`, `RecordDetailView.tsx`, `RelatedRecordActionsBridge.tsx`, `recordIdParam.ts`, `scripts/check-doc-component-types.mjs`, plus `.changeset/`, `packages/core/CHANGELOG.md`, `packages/core/package.json` and `packages/core/README.md` on `main`. Nothing built, run or re-run.

### Gate verdicts on the head

43 check-runs, all completed (waited in the foreground until the last shard reported, 20:07Z). 37 `success`, 3 `skipped` (coverage shards, dependabot), **3 `failure`, one cause**: Doc Component Type Check (job `109590992006`), Test (shard 5/8) (job `109590991703`) and the `Test` shard rollup (job `109596534216`, exit 3: "1 test shard(s) did not report success: Test (shard 5/8)"). Type Check, Lint, Build and E2E, Test (dist pins), Test shards 1 to 4 and 6 to 8, Doc Snippet Type Check, README Export Check, Changeset Bump Policy / Declaration / Claim Re-read / Fixed Group / Overwrite Report and Spec Main Shape Gate are green; shard 5 itself reports 1 failed, 6807 passed, 26 skipped, so `check:doc-snippets`, `check:readme-exports` and the full `app-shell` suite the dev declared to CI are answered green — the one red test is not an `app-shell` test.

The cause is this diff's. Doc Component Type Check's verdict line: `packages/core/README.md:195 [unregistered-doc-type] type 'json' (typescript)` on `config: { type: 'json' },` — a line this PR adds to the README's `captureUpdateUndoData` snippet. Shard 5's one red test is the gate's own repository pin, `scripts/__tests__/check-doc-component-types.test.ts` "the scan cannot collapse quietly, this repository is green" (`:1548`), which received exactly `unregistered-doc-type :: packages/core/README.md:195 :: json` where it expects `[]`. The README block at base carries no `type` literal; the same workflow is green on `main` (six most recent pushes) and on the twelve most recent PR runs. The gate names its own remedy: declare `json` in `DOC_TYPE_EXEMPTIONS` for `packages/core/README.md` with a reason naming the field data-type vocabulary — the table already carries that exact precedent (`content/docs/guide/record-edit-modes.md` exempts `picklist` as "ObjectStack object-metadata FIELD type inside a `fields` record, alongside `text` and `lookup`"). Neither `pnpm check:doc-types` nor `scripts/__tests__` was in the dev's gate list or narrowed test set, which is why the README growth reached CI red twice.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The capture rule** (`captureUpdateUndoData(writtenFields, rowRecord, fields)`, `ActionRunner.ts:996`) — RIGHT. The carry rule runs first, unchanged (`rowCarries` per written field, else `undefined`: objectui#10404 kept). Each value is then read off `toPredicateRecord(rowRecord, fields)`, whose relation set is `EXPANDABLE_FIELD_TYPES` (`lookup`, `master_detail`, `tree`, `user`), the set behind `isExpandableFieldType` and behind `buildExpandFields`, so what is collapsed is exactly what could have been expanded. A single relation holding `{ id }` or `{ _id }` collapses to its id (string or number, stringified); an array collapses element-wise with unexpanded members kept; a bare id, `null` and an absent key pass through; a `json` field is never touched whatever its shape, and `undefined` or `null` `fields` collapse nothing. `toPredicateRecord` returns a copy only when something collapsed, so the row is not mutated (pinned). No shape heuristic anywhere: triage's "never a shape heuristic" and "json holding `{ id, … }` restores the object unchanged" are met at the rule, not per surface. Accept-set change implied: none — `ActionDef`, the action schema and every authorable key are untouched.

2. **Console runtime writer** (`useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx:551`) — RIGHT. `obj = action.objectName || objApiName`; the field map is `withKnownObjects(objects, metadata.objects).find(name === obj)?.fields` after an awaited `metadata.ensureType('object')` whose rejection is caught — the same two-source lookup, in the same precedence (caller's list wins), that the param-collection path already used at `:246`. Under no `MetadataProvider`, `useMetadata()` answers the frozen no-op whose `ensureType` resolves to an empty list, so the await cannot throw. Pinned: the store lookup after `ensureType('object')`, with `objects` absent (the `ConsoleShell` root shape). Residual, not a defect: when `obj` is in neither list the writer falls back to the verbatim capture with no warning, although the grid built its `$expand` from `dataSource.getObjectSchema`; in the console both populations come from the same metadata server, so the gap is theoretical there and real only for an embedder that mounts the runtime with no store and an incomplete `objects`.

3. **Record page writer** (`RecordDetailView.tsx:996`) — RIGHT, and the tightest of the three: `objectDef?.fields` is the very map `buildExpandFields(objectDef?.fields)` used to request `$expand` (`:560`), so whenever the page expanded a relation it also holds the map that collapses it; no map means nothing was expanded and the verbatim capture is then correct. `isThisRecord` gating is unchanged.

4. **Runner writer** (`executeUpdateOperation`, `ActionRunner.ts:1714`) — RIGHT for the object the host names. `objectName = action.objectName || readContextObjectName(context)`; `readContextObjectFields(context, objectName)` answers `context.objectFields` only when `readContextObjectName(context) === objectName`, so one object's schema is never read against another object's row (pinned: the retargeted case keeps `config` as the object). Both console hosts publish the pair: the runtime spreads `objectFields: objectDef.fields` only beside an `objectName` (`:753`, pinned both ways), the page spreads it beside its `objectName` in its `ActionProvider` context (`:2730`, pinned). Silent fallback where a map WAS obtainable: yes, on the record page's related-list rows — `RelatedRecordActionsBridge` executes a child row action through the page's provider with `objectName: childObject` and `params: { _rowRecord: record }` (`:317`, `:319`, `:324`), the page holds every object in `objects`, but publishes only its own map, so the runner captures a child row verbatim. Judged under ③(a): a real residual of the same class, outside the pair contract this PR defines, carrier owed, not a breach of the card's pins (record page, grid row, json control, 10404 and 11082 pins: all green).

5. **The `objectFields` context key** — honest under the interface's own rule and the repo's precedent, and I do not require it declared on this head. `ActionContext` keeps `[key: string]: any` deliberately ("a runtime data bag whose keys are genuinely open … plus whatever a host passes", the `ActionDef` docblock at `:108`); `objectName` reached `readContextObjectName` the same way and shipped as a 17.5.0 **patch** (`9461dd3`, objectui#4292). The key is documented at its reader (`readContextObjectFields` docblock), in the rule's docblock, in the changeset and in both hosts. Two honest caveats for the seat: `pageVariables` is the counter-precedent (a host-published snapshot that IS declared), and `packages/core/README.md` documents `fields` on the rule but not the runner's `objectFields` pairing, so an embedder with a bare `ActionProvider` learns of it only from source or CHANGELOG. Declaring `objectFields?: FieldContainerLike` would be a widening (then `minor`, Clause-② yes); leaving it on the open bag is the `objectName` route. Either is defensible; the dev's choice is consistent with the surface it extends.

6. **Test edits** — RIGHT. The objectui#11082 export pin's six calls gain a `FIELDS` map with no expanded value; every assertion is unchanged, so it still pins the export identity and the carry rule. The new core pin covers every relation type via `EXPANDABLE_FIELD_TYPES` itself, `multiple` and mixed arrays, the `json` control by identity, both field-container shapes, no map, non-mutation, and the runner reading `objectFields` only for its own object. The two app-shell pins drive the real `RecordDetailView` (both writers) and a real `ObjectGrid` row inside the real `ConsoleActionRuntimeProvider` (api row action in the `ReassignLeadAction` shape, and an `operation: 'update'` row action), with Undo pressed on the real toast, asserting `dataSource.update(…, { account: 'a1' })`.

7. **Public-surface changes the diff implies**, named: (i) the signature of `captureUpdateUndoData` gains a REQUIRED third parameter (judged in ②); (ii) the runner reads a new context key `objectFields` (item 5); (iii) `packages/core/README.md` documents both `fields` and the relation rule (RIGHT in substance; the snippet is what trips the doc-type gate). No changeset-relevant surface beyond these; `ActionDef`, `@object-ui/types` and the spec mirrors are untouched.

### ② Semver level
